---
title: "Candidate fits for cumulative GPP allometry"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## Purpose

This report is a separate, non-destructive follow-on to Report 28. It uses the
same no-watershed-area cumulative GPP data, but starts by comparing four ways
to describe the cumulative GPP–area relationship:

1. Linear regression in log10-log10 space.
2. Quadratic polynomial regression in log10-log10 space.
3. LOESS in log10-log10 space.
4. One-breakpoint segmented regression in log10-log10 space.

The four panels use the same data and log10 axes. The orange curve is the
prediction from the model named in that panel.

```{r packages-and-paths}
source("00_setup.R")

pacman::p_load(knitr, segmented, ggrepel)

dir_processed <- "../data/processed"
path_fits <- file.path(dir_processed, "18_refit_allometry_results.csv")
path_huc8_areas <- file.path(dir_processed, "04c_huc08_summary.csv")
path_scatter_input <- file.path(dir_processed, "18_refit_no_uparea_scatter_input.rds")
```

## 1. Read the no-area-model GPP data

```{r read-data}
gpp_fits <- read_csv(path_fits, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(
    model == "without_uparea",
    metabolism == "GPP",
    is.finite(slope),
    is.finite(intercept)
  )

median_huc8_fit <- gpp_fits %>%
  summarise(
    median_slope = median(slope),
    median_intercept = median(intercept),
    n_huc8_month_fits = n(),
    n_huc8 = n_distinct(huc)
  )

kable(median_huc8_fit, digits = 3)

scatter_data <- readRDS(path_scatter_input) %>%
  filter(metabolism == "GPP") %>%
  transmute(
    cumulative_area_km2,
    cumulative_flux_g_o2_d,
    log_area = log10(cumulative_area_km2),
    log_gpp = log10(cumulative_flux_g_o2_d)
  )
```

## 2. Fit four candidate relationships

All models are fit on the log10-transformed variables. That is why a linear
model in this report appears as a straight line on the log10-log10 plots.

```{r fit-candidate-models}
linear_fit <- lm(log_gpp ~ log_area, data = scatter_data)

polynomial_fit <- lm(
  log_gpp ~ poly(log_area, degree = 2, raw = TRUE),
  data = scatter_data
)

# LOESS on a fixed subset is visually stable while avoiding an unnecessarily
# expensive fit to every reach-month record.
set.seed(29)
loess_data <- scatter_data %>%
  slice_sample(n = min(20000, nrow(scatter_data)))

loess_fit <- loess(
  log_gpp ~ log_area,
  data = loess_data,
  span = 0.4
)

# One breakpoint lets the log-log slope differ above versus below that area.
segmented_fit <- segmented(
  linear_fit,
  seg.Z = ~log_area,
  psi = median(scatter_data$log_area),
  control = seg.control(display = FALSE)
)

fit_grid <- tibble(
  log_area = seq(
    min(scatter_data$log_area),
    max(scatter_data$log_area),
    length.out = 500
  )
) %>%
  mutate(cumulative_area_km2 = 10 ^ log_area)

candidate_predictions <- bind_rows(
  fit_grid %>%
    transmute(
      model = "Linear",
      cumulative_area_km2,
      cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d = 10 ^ predict(linear_fit, newdata = fit_grid)
    ),
  fit_grid %>%
    transmute(
      model = "Quadratic polynomial",
      cumulative_area_km2,
      cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d = 10 ^ predict(polynomial_fit, newdata = fit_grid)
    ),
  fit_grid %>%
    transmute(
      model = "LOESS",
      cumulative_area_km2,
      cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d = 10 ^ predict(loess_fit, newdata = fit_grid)
    ),
  fit_grid %>%
    transmute(
      model = "Segmented",
      cumulative_area_km2,
      cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d = 10 ^ predict(segmented_fit, newdata = fit_grid)
    )
) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = c(
    "Linear", "Quadratic polynomial", "LOESS", "Segmented"
  )))

segmented_breakpoint_km2 <- 10 ^ segmented_fit$psi[1, "Est."]

tibble(
  model = c("Linear", "Quadratic polynomial", "LOESS", "Segmented"),
  fit_on = c("All reach-months", "All reach-months", "20,000 reach-month sample", "All reach-months"),
  segmented_breakpoint_km2 = c(NA, NA, NA, segmented_breakpoint_km2)
) %>%
  kable(digits = 1)
```

```{r plot-candidate-fits, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
ggplot(scatter_data, aes(cumulative_area_km2, cumulative_flux_g_o2_d)) +
  geom_hex(bins = 75) +
  geom_line(
    data = candidate_predictions,
    aes(x = cumulative_area_km2, y = cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "#D55E00",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~model, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number_auto()) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number_auto()) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "D", trans = "log10", name = "Reach-month count") +
  labs(
    title = "Candidate cumulative GPP allometry fits",
    x = expression("Cumulative upstream area (km"^2*")"),
    y = expression("Cumulative GPP (g O"[2]*" d"^-1*")")
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

<!-- Segmented plotting code is defined here, then executed at the end. -->

```{r prepare-segmented-global-references, eval=FALSE}
segmented_curve <- candidate_predictions_normalized %>% filter(model == "Segmented")
segmented_huc8_points <- candidate_huc8_predictions_normalized %>% filter(model == "Segmented")

# Segmented regression remains linear beyond its final breakpoint, so its
# terminal segment supplies the dashed extension to the global basin areas.
segmented_extension <- tibble(
  cumulative_area_km2 = seq(
    max(segmented_curve$cumulative_area_km2),
    max(global_rivers$cumulative_area_km2),
    length.out = 150
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    log_area = log10(cumulative_area_km2),
    predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d =
      10 ^ predict(segmented_fit, newdata = tibble(log_area)) / cumulative_area_km2
  )

segmented_us_mouths <- selected_us_mouths %>%
  dplyr::select(river, comid, cumulative_area_km2) %>%
  mutate(
    log_area = log10(cumulative_area_km2),
    predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d =
      10 ^ predict(segmented_fit, newdata = tibble(log_area)) / cumulative_area_km2
  )

segmented_global_rivers <- global_rivers %>%
  dplyr::select(river, cumulative_area_km2) %>%
  mutate(
    log_area = log10(cumulative_area_km2),
    predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d =
      10 ^ predict(segmented_fit, newdata = tibble(log_area)) / cumulative_area_km2
  )

make_segmented_global_plot <- function(log_axes = FALSE) {
  plot <- ggplot(
    scatter_data,
    aes(x = cumulative_area_km2, y = cumulative_flux_g_o2_d / cumulative_area_km2)
  ) +
    geom_hex(bins = 75) +
    geom_line(data = segmented_curve,
              aes(cumulative_area_km2, predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#009E73", linewidth = 1.1) +
    geom_line(data = segmented_extension,
              aes(cumulative_area_km2, predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#009E73", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1.1) +
    geom_point(data = segmented_huc8_points,
               aes(cumulative_area_km2, predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black", alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5) +
    geom_point(data = segmented_us_mouths,
               aes(cumulative_area_km2, predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 21, fill = "white", colour = "#0072B2", stroke = 1.2, size = 4.5) +
    geom_text_repel(data = segmented_us_mouths,
                    aes(cumulative_area_km2, predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d, label = river),
                    inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#0072B2", size = 3.5, seed = 29) +
    geom_point(data = segmented_global_rivers,
               aes(cumulative_area_km2, predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 21, fill = "white", colour = "#6A3D9A", stroke = 1.3, size = 4.5) +
    geom_text_repel(data = segmented_global_rivers,
                    aes(cumulative_area_km2, predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d, label = river),
                    inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#6A3D9A", size = 3.5, seed = 29) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "D", trans = "log10", name = "Reach-month count") +
    labs(
      title = "Segmented area-normalized cumulative GPP with global river references",
      subtitle = "Solid green = fitted segmented regression; dashed green = terminal-segment extension",
      x = expression("Cumulative upstream area (km"^2*")"),
      y = expression("Cumulative GPP / upstream area (g O"[2]*" km"^-2*" d"^-1*")")
    ) +
    theme_bw()

  if (log_axes) {
    plot + scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number_auto()) +
      scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number_auto())
  } else {
    plot
  }
}
```

```{r final-global-segmented-panel, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, eval=FALSE}
print(make_segmented_global_plot())
```

```{r final-global-segmented-panel-loglog, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, eval=FALSE}
print(make_segmented_global_plot(log_axes = TRUE))
```

<!--
Global drainage areas are taken from the [Government of Canada river-area
table](https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/water-overview/sources/rivers.html).
The Amazon, Congo, and Ob–Irtysh have reported drainage areas larger than the
modeled Mississippi mouth area used here. These global points are predictions
on the extrapolated LOESS trend, not observations of GPP outside CONUS.
-->

```{r prepare-global-river-references, eval=FALSE}
global_rivers <- tibble(
  river = c("Amazon", "Congo", "Ob-Irtysh"),
  cumulative_area_km2 = c(6915000, 3680000, 2990000)
)

# LOESS cannot extrapolate beyond its training range. Continue its terminal
# log-log slope as a dashed extension, solely for the global reference points.
terminal_loess_data <- loess_curve %>%
  slice_tail(n = 30) %>%
  mutate(
    log_area = log10(cumulative_area_km2),
    log_gpp = log10(predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d)
  )

terminal_loess_fit <- lm(log_gpp ~ log_area, data = terminal_loess_data)

loess_extension <- tibble(
  cumulative_area_km2 = seq(
    max(loess_curve$cumulative_area_km2),
    max(global_rivers$cumulative_area_km2),
    length.out = 150
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d = 10 ^ predict(
      terminal_loess_fit,
      newdata = tibble(log_area = log10(cumulative_area_km2))
    )
  )

global_rivers <- global_rivers %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d = 10 ^ predict(
      terminal_loess_fit,
      newdata = tibble(log_area = log10(cumulative_area_km2))
    )
  )

selected_us_mouths <- river_mouths %>%
  filter(river %in% c("Mississippi", "Columbia"))
```

```{r plot-loess-with-global-rivers, fig.width=10, fig.height=8, include=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
ggplot(
  scatter_data,
  aes(
    x = cumulative_area_km2,
    y = cumulative_flux_g_o2_d / cumulative_area_km2
  )
) +
  geom_hex(bins = 75) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black") +
  geom_line(
    data = loess_curve,
    aes(x = cumulative_area_km2, y = predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "#D55E00",
    linewidth = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = loess_extension,
    aes(x = cumulative_area_km2, y = predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "#D55E00",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = loess_huc8_points,
    aes(x = cumulative_area_km2, y = predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "black",
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 1.5
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = selected_us_mouths,
    aes(x = cumulative_area_km2, y = predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    shape = 21,
    fill = "white",
    colour = "#0072B2",
    stroke = 1.2,
    size = 4.5
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = selected_us_mouths,
    aes(x = cumulative_area_km2, y = predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d, label = river),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "#0072B2",
    size = 3.5,
    seed = 29
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = global_rivers,
    aes(x = cumulative_area_km2, y = predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    shape = 21,
    fill = "white",
    colour = "#6A3D9A",
    stroke = 1.3,
    size = 4.5
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = global_rivers,

    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "#6A3D9A",
    size = 3.5,
    seed = 29
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "D", trans = "log10", name = "Reach-month count") +
  labs(
    title = "LOESS area-normalized cumulative GPP with global river references",
    subtitle = "Solid orange = fitted LOESS; dashed orange = terminal-slope extrapolation",
    x = expression("Cumulative upstream area (km"^2*")"),
    y = expression("Cumulative GPP / upstream area (g O"[2]*" km"^-2*" d"^-1*")")
  ) +

```

## 3. Evaluate each candidate function at HUC8 upstream areas

```{r project-candidates-to-huc8-areas}
# This is the area vector to which each candidate function is applied.
huc8_projection_areas <- read_csv(path_huc8_areas, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(
    huc8 = str_pad(as.character(huc8), width = 8, pad = "0"),
    huc8_name,
    cumulative_area_km2 = max_uparea_km2
  ) %>%
  filter(is.finite(cumulative_area_km2), cumulative_area_km2 > 0) %>%
  mutate(log_area = log10(cumulative_area_km2))

# Each fit receives only `log_area`, the predictor used to fit the models.
# The resulting vectors are then attached to the same HUC8 area table.
huc8_newdata <- huc8_projection_areas %>%
  dplyr::select(log_area)

linear_huc8_prediction <- predict(linear_fit, newdata = huc8_newdata)
polynomial_huc8_prediction <- predict(polynomial_fit, newdata = huc8_newdata)
loess_huc8_prediction <- predict(loess_fit, newdata = huc8_newdata)
segmented_huc8_prediction <- predict(segmented_fit, newdata = huc8_newdata)

candidate_huc8_predictions <- bind_rows(
  huc8_projection_areas %>%
    transmute(
      huc8, huc8_name, cumulative_area_km2,
      model = "Linear",
      predicted_cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d = 10 ^ linear_huc8_prediction
    ),
  huc8_projection_areas %>%
    transmute(
      huc8, huc8_name, cumulative_area_km2,
      model = "Quadratic polynomial",
      predicted_cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d = 10 ^ polynomial_huc8_prediction
    ),
  huc8_projection_areas %>%
    transmute(
      huc8, huc8_name, cumulative_area_km2,
      model = "LOESS",
      predicted_cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d = 10 ^ loess_huc8_prediction
    ),
  huc8_projection_areas %>%
    transmute(
      huc8, huc8_name, cumulative_area_km2,
      model = "Segmented",
      predicted_cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d = 10 ^ segmented_huc8_prediction
    )
) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = levels(candidate_predictions$model)))
```

```{r plot-huc8-projections, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
ggplot(candidate_predictions,
       aes(cumulative_area_km2, cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(
    data = candidate_huc8_predictions,
    aes(y = predicted_cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d),
    colour = "black",
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 1.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~model, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number_auto()) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number_auto()) +
  labs(
    title = "Candidate cumulative GPP functions evaluated at HUC8 areas",
    x = expression("Maximum upstream area in HUC8 (km"^2*")"),
    y = expression("Predicted cumulative GPP (g O"[2]*" d"^-1*")")
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## 4. Area-normalized candidate projections

For each candidate, cumulative GPP is divided by the same cumulative upstream
area plotted on the x-axis. The resulting y-axis is g O~2~ km^-2^ d^-1^.

```{r normalize-candidate-projections}
candidate_predictions_normalized <- candidate_predictions %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d =
      cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d / cumulative_area_km2
  )

candidate_huc8_predictions_normalized <- candidate_huc8_predictions %>%
  mutate(
    predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d =
      predicted_cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d / cumulative_area_km2
  )
```

```{r plot-area-normalized-candidates, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
ggplot(candidate_predictions_normalized,
       aes(cumulative_area_km2, predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(
    data = candidate_huc8_predictions_normalized,
    aes(y = predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
    colour = "black",
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 1.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~model, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number_auto()) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number_auto()) +
  labs(
    title = "Candidate cumulative GPP functions normalized by upstream area",
    x = expression("Maximum upstream area in HUC8 (km"^2*")"),
    y = expression("Predicted cumulative GPP / upstream area (g O"[2]*" km"^-2*" d"^-1*")")
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## 7. LOESS-only version of Section 6 with selected river mouths

```{r prepare-mouth-reference-points}
river_mouths <- tibble(
  river = c("Mississippi", "Ohio", "Columbia", "Rio Grande"),
  comid = c("74072169", "74050625", "78018922", "75025589"),
  cumulative_area_km2 = c(2893087.8, 519221.5, 651499.3, 504948.2)
) %>%
  mutate(
    log_area = log10(cumulative_area_km2),
    predicted_cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d = 10 ^ predict(loess_fit, newdata = tibble(log_area)),
    predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d = predicted_cumulative_gpp_g_o2_d / cumulative_area_km2
  )

loess_curve <- candidate_predictions_normalized %>% filter(model == "LOESS")
loess_huc8_points <- candidate_huc8_predictions_normalized %>% filter(model == "LOESS")
```

```{r plot-final-loess-panel, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
ggplot(scatter_data,
       aes(cumulative_area_km2, cumulative_flux_g_o2_d / cumulative_area_km2)) +
  geom_hex(bins = 75) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black") +
  geom_line(data = loess_curve,
            aes(cumulative_area_km2, predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(data = loess_huc8_points,
             aes(cumulative_area_km2, predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black", alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(data = river_mouths,
             aes(cumulative_area_km2, predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 21, fill = "white", colour = "#0072B2",
             stroke = 1.2, size = 4.5) +
  geom_text_repel(data = river_mouths,
                  aes(cumulative_area_km2, predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d, label = river),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#0072B2", size = 3.5, seed = 29) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "D", trans = "log10", name = "Reach-month count") +
  labs(
    title = "LOESS panel from Section 6 with selected river mouths",
    subtitle = "Linear axes; dashed line = 1:1; hollow blue points = LOESS mouth references",
    x = expression("Cumulative upstream area (km"^2*")"),
    y = expression("Cumulative GPP / upstream area (g O"[2]*" km"^-2*" d"^-1*")")
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## 8. LOESS panel extended to global rivers larger than the Mississippi

This global-context version retains only the Columbia and Mississippi U.S.
mouth markers. Purple hollow points are the Amazon, Congo, and Ob–Irtysh on
the dashed extrapolated extension.

```{r prepare-final-global-river-references}
global_rivers <- tibble(
  river = c("Amazon", "Congo", "Ob-Irtysh"),
  cumulative_area_km2 = c(6915000, 3680000, 2990000)
)

# LOESS does not extrapolate. Extend its terminal log-log trend only to give
# the global reference areas a transparent, explicitly extrapolated position.
terminal_loess_data <- loess_curve %>%
  slice_tail(n = 30) %>%
  mutate(
    log_area = log10(cumulative_area_km2),
    log_gpp = log10(predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d)
  )
terminal_loess_fit <- lm(log_gpp ~ log_area, data = terminal_loess_data)

loess_extension <- tibble(
  cumulative_area_km2 = seq(
    max(loess_curve$cumulative_area_km2),
    max(global_rivers$cumulative_area_km2),
    length.out = 150
  )
) %>%
  mutate(predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d = 10 ^ predict(
    terminal_loess_fit,
    newdata = tibble(log_area = log10(cumulative_area_km2))
  ))

global_rivers <- global_rivers %>%
  mutate(predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d = 10 ^ predict(
    terminal_loess_fit,
    newdata = tibble(log_area = log10(cumulative_area_km2))
  ))

selected_us_mouths <- river_mouths %>%
  filter(river %in% c("Mississippi", "Columbia"))
```

```{r final-global-loess-panel, ref.label='plot-loess-with-global-rivers', fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
```


```{r final-global-loess-panel-loglog, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
ggplot(
  scatter_data,
  aes(
    x = cumulative_area_km2,
    y = cumulative_flux_g_o2_d / cumulative_area_km2
  )
) +
  geom_hex(bins = 75) +

  ) +

  ) +
  geom_point(

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 1.5
  ) +
  geom_point(

    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    shape = 21,

    stroke = 1.2,
    size = 4.5
  ) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = selected_us_mouths,
    aes(x = cumulative_area_km2, y = predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d, label = river),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "#0072B2",
    size = 3.5,
    seed = 29
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = global_rivers,
    aes(x = cumulative_area_km2, y = predicted_gpp_g_o2_km2_d),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    seed = 29
  ) +
```
